resume.text:
Laura M. Brennan
laura.brennan@email.com | 555-482-1937 | Seattle, WA | linkedin.com/in/laurambrennan

Senior UX Designer with over 12 years of experience leading design teams and driving user-centered strategy for digital products. Proven track record of managing cross-functional teams and budgets while delivering scalable design solutions that enhance engagement and customer satisfaction. Adept at balancing business goals with user needs to create impactful experiences in fast-paced environments.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Lead UX Designer / Design Manager
BrightWave Technologies, Seattle, WA
March 2018 - Present
- Manage a team of 8 UX designers and researchers, overseeing project roadmaps and design resource allocation for multiple client-facing web and mobile products
- Own the UX budget and vendor contracts, optimizing spend to support research initiatives and tool acquisitions
- Collaborate with product and engineering leadership to define UX strategy that aligns with company growth plans and enhances product usability
- Spearheaded redesign of the flagship SaaS platform, improving user retention by 15% within six months of launch through iterative user testing and feedback incorporation
- Mentor junior designers and facilitate regular design critiques to elevate team skills and output quality
- Led cross-team workshops to establish company-wide design standards and accessibility guidelines

Senior UX Designer
Veridian Health Systems, Bellevue, WA
June 2014 - February 2018
- Partnered with product managers and developers to design patient-facing and clinician portals serving over 200,000 monthly users
- Conducted usability studies and heuristic evaluations to identify friction points, resulting in interface improvements that reduced support calls by approximately 12%
- Balanced multiple project timelines while coordinating with external agencies to deliver cohesive user experiences
- Introduced new prototyping tools that accelerated design iteration cycles by 30%
- Contributed to strategic planning by presenting quarterly UX performance insights to executive leadership
- Led training sessions on user-centered design principles for cross-departmental teams

UX Designer
Nimbus Media Group, Portland, OR
January 2010 - May 2014
- Designed interactive experiences for web and mobile applications targeting diverse client industries, including finance and retail
- Collaborated with product owners to translate business requirements into wireframes, mockups, and high-fidelity prototypes
- Participated in user research activities such as interviews and surveys to guide design decisions
- Worked with front-end developers to ensure design feasibility and consistency
- Supported the adoption of responsive design standards across projects
- Assisted with client presentations and design documentation

EDUCATION

Bachelor of Arts in Graphic Design
University of Washington, Seattle, WA
2005 - 2009

SKILLS

User Experience Strategy | Team Leadership | UX Research & Testing | Interaction Design | UX Budget Management | Prototyping (Figma, Sketch) | Cross-functional Collaboration | Accessibility Standards | Design Systems | Agile Methodologies | Data-driven Design | Mentorship and Training

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“- Collaborate with product and engineering leadership to define UX strategy that aligns with company growth plans and enhances product usability”

REWRITE

Collaborate with product and engineering leadership to define UX strategy for company growth plans and improve product usability; result: [measurable usability or business result]

Add the decision, product area, or measurable result tied to this strategy work.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

How did you balance company growth plans with usability needs at BrightWave?

Why it may help: The resume names both priorities but not the tradeoff or decision you made.

QUESTION 02

How did design standards scale across teams, products, or locations?

Why it may help: The company-wide standards workshops suggest broad reach, but the scale is not stated.

QUESTION 03

What quality risk did you manage while coordinating multiple timelines and external agencies?

Why it may help: This would show how you protected user experience when delivery pressure increased.

QUESTION 04

Which prototyping tools replaced the prior process, and what enabled the 30% faster iteration?

Why it may help: The result is useful, but the mechanism behind it is unclear.

QUESTION 05

How did product, engineering, and research leaders resolve disagreements during the SaaS redesign?

Why it may help: The redesign shows ownership, while the cross-functional decision process remains hidden.

KEEP THESE

The parts already earning trust.
01

Managing 8 UX designers and researchers gives the current role a clear people-leadership anchor.

02

The flagship SaaS redesign connects iterative user testing to a 15% retention improvement within six months.

03

Veridian’s portals served over 200,000 monthly users, giving the healthcare work meaningful product scale.

ROLE DIRECTION

Where this story reads strongest.

Position yourself around UX leadership for SaaS and complex digital products, using the 8-person team and 15% retention result near the top. Add budget, product scale, and design-system adoption details to distinguish design management from senior individual-contributor work.

BEST FIT NOW

UX Design Manager

Director of UX
